name: Apical Resection
meta_title: Apical Resection (Apicoectomy): Advanced Root-End Dental Surgery
meta_description: Learn about apical resection, or apicoectomy, a specialized dental procedure to treat persistent root canal infections and save your natural tooth from extraction. Discover the benefits, procedure details, and recovery.
meta_keywords: apical resection, apicoectomy, root-end surgery, dental surgery, endodontic surgery, save a tooth, root canal failure, persistent tooth infection, dental microsurgery

what_is.heading: What is Apical Resection? Saving Your Natural Tooth
paragraphs: An apical resection, also known as an apicoectomy or root-end surgery, is a specialized surgical procedure performed to treat a persistent infection or inflammation at the very tip (apex) of a tooth's root. This procedure is typically recommended when a standard root canal treatment has failed to resolve the issue or is not possible.

During an apicoectomy, our dental surgeon makes a small incision in the gum tissue to expose the underlying bone and the root tip. The infected tissue around the root is removed, along with the very end of the root itself. A small filling is then placed at the end of the root to seal the canal and prevent reinfection.

why_needed.heading: Why is an Apicoectomy Necessary?
paragraphs: This microsurgical procedure is a vital tool for saving a tooth that would otherwise need to be extracted, allowing it to function for many more years. It is often the last resort to effectively resolve a chronic infection when other non-surgical options are not viable, preserving your natural tooth structure.
